heroHeadline: Peru Election Crisis: Fujimori vs. Sánchez in June 7 Runoff After 35-Day Post-Election Turmoil
heroSubtitle: Peru's 2026 election — a contest between Keiko Fujimori (17%) and leftist Roberto Sánchez (12%) — was certified only after a 35-day crisis: ballot delivery failures, ONPE director raids, fraud claims by 3rd-place López Aliaga, and a JNE-mandated IT audit. This follows eight heads of state in under a decade, Pedro Castillo's conviction for conspiracy for rebellion, and Dina Boluarte's 122–0 removal in October 2025.
footerNote: Data sourced from CVR Informe Final (2003), ONPE/JNE official results, BCRP, INEI, Inter-American Court of Human Rights, major Peruvian outlets (El Comercio, La República, Infobae Perú), and international news. Casualty figures for 1980–2000 conflict use CVR multiple systems estimation methodology.
